name: Castelo de São Jorge
notes: Hilltop castle with panoramic views over Lisbon; mix of ramparts and some indoor areas.

name: Time Out Market Lisboa
notes: Large indoor food hall with many Lisbon restaurants under one roof.

name: Jerónimos Monastery
notes: Iconic monastery in Belém; cloisters and church, good mix of indoor and outdoor.

name: Oceanário de Lisboa
notes: Big indoor aquarium; perfect rainy-day or too-hot-day activity.

name: LX Factory
notes: Trendy complex with shops, cafés, and street art; some indoor, some outdoor.

name: Praia de Carcavelos
notes: Wide sandy beach with surf, promenade, and cafés; best in good weather.

name: Cabo da Roca
notes: Westernmost point of continental Europe; big views, very exposed to wind.

name: Castelo de Sesimbra
notes: Hilltop castle with sea views over Sesimbra; mostly outdoor, sunny-day activity.

name: Parque Natural da Arrábida (viewpoints)
notes: Scenic drives and viewpoints over turquoise water; half-day sunny mission.

name: Mercado do Livramento
notes: Classic Portuguese market hall; best in the morning for fish and tiles.

name: O Passo Coffee House
notes: Cowork and coffee house; great for breakfast, light lunch, or laptop time.

name: Solo Café
notes: Brunch and coffee spot by the garden; good lazy-morning option.

name: Coffee T Food House
notes: Casual café/restaurant; easy breakfast, lunch, or simple dinner nearby.

name: Casa da Dízima
notes: Upscale Portuguese with river views; best for long lunches or nice dinners.

name: Pátio Antico Restaurante Italiano
notes: Italian in Paço de Arcos; solid pasta/pizza for lunch or dinner.

name: Restaurante Zé Varunca
notes: Alentejo-style Portuguese; hearty traditional meals.

name: O Pastus
notes: Portuguese & grilled dishes; reliable local lunch/dinner spot.

name: Mercado de Campo de Ourique
notes: Smaller, local-feeling food market; indoor and easy on rainy days.

name: Vida de Tasca
notes: Lively tasca with modern Portuguese petiscos in Lisbon center.

name: SushiCafé Oeiras Parque
notes: Mall sushi in Oeiras Parque; easy indoor option on bad-weather days.

name: La Plage Carcavelos
notes: Beachfront restaurant at Carcavelos; good for lunch, sunset drinks, or dinner.

name: Soya Noodle Bar Carcavelos
notes: Asian / noodle bar near Carcavelos beach; strong reviews, cozy indoor spot.

name: Santini Carcavelos
notes: Famous Portuguese ice cream chain by the beach; good quick stop after a walk.

name: Passeio Marítimo de Oeiras
notes: Seafront promenade great for a sunny walk or run from Paço/Oeiras towards Caxias.

name: Paredão Paço de Arcos–Carcavelos
notes: Flat oceanfront walk between Paço de Arcos and Carcavelos along the sea wall.

name: Parque dos Poetas
notes: Large park with sculptures and viewpoints; easy urban green space.

name: Guincho Coastal Walk
notes: Windy Atlantic coastline around Guincho; half-day walk with big views.

name: Monsanto Forest Park Trail
notes: Trails and viewpoints in Lisbon’s big forest park; quick “hike” without leaving the city.

name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
notes: Tile museum with cloisters and classic azulejos; solid indoor option.

name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
notes: Top-tier art museum with gardens; good half-day culture + park combo.

name: MAAT – Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
notes: Striking riverside museum with rooftop views over the Tagus.

name: Quake – Museu do Terramoto de Lisboa
notes: Immersive museum about the 1755 Lisbon earthquake; fully indoor.

name: Museu da Marinha
notes: Navy and maritime museum in Belém; easy to combine with Jerónimos.

name: Rijksmuseum
notes: The Netherlands' greatest museum, home to Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer's Milkmaid. Pre-book timed entry tickets.

name: Van Gogh Museum
notes: World's largest collection of Van Gogh works including Sunflowers and The Bedroom. Pre-book timed entry mandatory.

name: Anne Frank House
notes: The hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. One of Amsterdam's most moving and essential visits; pre-book well in advance.

name: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
notes: World-class modern and contemporary art and design museum on Museumplein. Open 365 days a year.

name: NEMO Science Museum
notes: Interactive science museum in a distinctive green ship-shaped building with a rooftop terrace offering great canal views. Great for families.

name: EYE Filmmuseum
notes: Striking modern film museum in Amsterdam Noord with exhibitions, screenings, and a waterfront café. Free ferry from Central Station.

name: Artis Royal Zoo
notes: The oldest zoo in the Netherlands, located in the charming Plantage district. Includes an aquarium, planetarium, and Micropia (microorganism museum).

name: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam
notes: Beautiful 17th-century botanical garden with tropical glasshouses and a butterfly greenhouse. Peaceful refuge near the zoo.

name: Heineken Experience
notes: Interactive brewery tour in the original 1867 Heineken brewery in De Pijp. Includes tasting; popular with groups.

name: Begijnhof
notes: Hidden medieval courtyard tucked behind the Spui, one of Amsterdam's most tranquil and photogenic spots. Free to enter.

name: Westerkerk
notes: Amsterdam's most iconic church with the tallest tower in the city, next to the Anne Frank House. Rembrandt is buried here.

name: Amsterdam Canal Ring (Grachtengordel)
notes: UNESCO World Heritage 17th-century canal ring; the Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht are essential walking routes.

name: Jordaan Neighborhood
notes: Amsterdam's most charming neighbourhood: narrow streets, hidden hofjes, boutiques, galleries, and cozy brown cafes. Best explored on foot.

name: De Pijp Neighborhood
notes: Vibrant multicultural neighbourhood south of centre, home to Albert Cuypmarkt, diverse restaurants, and a lively café scene.

name: Vondelpark
notes: Amsterdam's beloved central park: rose garden, open-air theatre, ponds, and plenty of café terraces. Lively on sunny days.

name: Amsterdamse Bos
notes: Vast forest park south of Amsterdam, three times larger than New York's Central Park. Great for cycling, rowing, and long walks.

name: Albert Cuypmarkt
notes: The largest outdoor market in the Netherlands with 260 stalls selling food, clothes, and daily goods. The beating heart of De Pijp.

name: Noordermarkt
notes: Jordaan market: Monday flea market, Saturday organic farmers' market. Winkel 43's famous apple pie is steps away.

name: Waterlooplein Flea Market
notes: Amsterdam's oldest flea market, open six days a week. Great for vintage clothes, antiques, and secondhand curiosities.

name: The Pantry
notes: Beloved Amsterdam institution near Leidseplein serving hearty traditional Dutch dishes like stamppot and erwtensoep in a cosy homely setting.

name: Blue Pepper Restaurant
notes: Widely regarded as Amsterdam's finest Indonesian restaurant, serving an elegant four-course rijsttafel. Reservations essential.

name: Restaurant Blauw
notes: Popular Indonesian restaurant in Oud-Zuid serving generous rijsttafels and a vegan option. Always busy; book ahead.

name: Winkel 43
notes: The famous corner café on the Noordermarkt, known across Amsterdam for its exceptional homemade apple pie heaped with fresh cream.

name: Bocca Coffee
notes: One of Amsterdam's most respected specialty roasters near Vondelpark, known for exceptional single-origin coffees and barista training.

name: Back to Black Coffee
notes: Third-wave specialty coffee roastery and café on the Weteringstraat; part coffee bar, part concept store with strong brunch food.

name: L'Abeille Pastry & Coffee
notes: Michelin-pedigreed pâtisserie in Amsterdam East praised for Amsterdam's best croissants. Also runs pastry workshops.

name: Fort Negen
notes: Artisan bakery in Amsterdam West near Vondelpark that draws long morning queues for its exceptional sourdough loaves and pastries.

name: Farine Boulangerie & Café
notes: Authentic French boulangerie in Bos en Lommer with Paris-quality croissants and fresh pastries baked daily. Cosy neighbourhood gem.

name: Café Hoppe
notes: One of Amsterdam's oldest brown cafes (1670) on the Spui, a national monument. Locals crowd its terrace on sunny days for Dutch beer and jenever.

name: Café 't Papeneiland
notes: Classic Jordaan brown cafe at the Prinsengracht, dating to 1642. Famously cosy with Delft tiles and its own excellent apple pie.

name: Café 't Smalle
notes: Historic Jordaan proeflokaal (tasting house) in a former jenever distillery from 1780. Lovely canalside terrace in summer.

name: Café Nol
notes: The most famous brown cafe in the Jordaan, known for Dutch folk music (volkszangers) and a festive sing-along atmosphere most nights.

name: Brouwerij 't IJ
notes: Amsterdam's most famous craft brewery, housed inside a working windmill near the Eastern Docklands. Organic beers and a sunny terrace.

name: Concertgebouw
notes: One of the world's most acoustically perfect concert halls. Free Wednesday lunchtime concerts make it accessible to all visitors.

name: Dam Square
notes: Amsterdam's historic main square with the Royal Palace and National Monument. Central hub for sightseeing and people-watching.

name: Red Light District (De Wallen)
notes: Amsterdam's medieval De Wallen neighbourhood, most famous by night but also home to the Oude Kerk (oldest church) and excellent restaurants.

name: Café Chris
notes: The oldest brown café in the Jordaan (opened 1624), a tiny gem with dark wooden beams. The builders of Westerkerk drank their wages here.

name: Amsterdam Noord & NDSM Wharf
notes: Post-industrial creative hub on the IJ waterfront, home to street art, markets, studios, and the Pllek beach bar. Free ferry from Central Station.

name: Keukenhof Gardens
notes: The world's largest flower garden with 7 million tulips, open only mid-March to mid-May. About 25 minutes by bus from Hoofddorp station.

name: Haarlemmermeerse Bos
notes: Large recreational forest park near Hoofddorp with a lake, walking and cycling paths, and the Big Spotters Hill with views of Schiphol runway.

name: Spottersplaats Polderbaan
notes: Official plane-spotting area at the end of Schiphol's Polderbaan runway in Vijfhuizen. Planes pass overhead at very low altitude; free to visit.

name: Zaanse Schans
notes: Open-air windmill village 20 min from Schiphol by train. Working historic windmills, wooden shoe workshops, and cheese farms on the River Zaan.

name: Restaurant Den Burgh
notes: One of Hoofddorp's most popular restaurants offering Dutch, seafood, and European cuisine. Consistently well-reviewed by locals and hotel guests.

name: Stadspark Hoofddorp
notes: Well-maintained urban park in the centre of Hoofddorp, ideal for a short walk or picnic, just minutes from local hotels.

name: Escape World Hoofddorp
notes: Popular escape room venue in Hoofddorp with multiple themed rooms. Perfect rainy-day activity close to the airport hotels.

name: Grand Café De Lightenvoorde
notes: Popular grand café in Hoofddorp town centre serving Dutch café food from breakfast through dinner, with a pleasant outdoor terrace.

name: Rijksmuseum Schiphol
notes: Free mini-museum inside Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (airside, Holland Boulevard) displaying a rotating selection of Dutch Golden Age masterworks.

name: De Pannenkoeken Paviljoen
notes: Traditional Dutch pancake restaurant in the Haarlemmermeerse Bos park, serving both sweet and savoury pannenkoeken in a scenic forest setting.

name: Brouwerij De Prael
notes: Social enterprise craft brewery in the Red Light District making Dutch-themed beers named after local legends. Tasting room and tours available.

name: IJ-Kantine
notes: Waterfront café-restaurant on the IJ in Amsterdam Noord with a large sunny terrace. Accessible via free ferry from Central Station.

name: Pllek Beach Bar
notes: Trendy beach bar at the NDSM Wharf in Amsterdam Noord built from shipping containers, with a sandy waterfront terrace. Very popular on sunny days.

name: Foodhallen Amsterdam
notes: Indoor street food market in a converted tram depot in Oud-West, with around 20 food stalls and a lively bar scene. Excellent for groups.

name: Café de Jaren
notes: Grand and spacious Amsterdam café on the Nieuwe Doelenstraat with a spectacular canal-side terrace. Great for breakfast, lunch, or drinks.

name: Mama Makan
notes: Indonesian restaurant in the Hyatt Regency with a botanical interior. Chef Rosmina's five-round rijsttafel is one of Amsterdam's finest.

name: Sarphatipark
notes: De Pijp's beloved neighbourhood park, a smaller and more local alternative to Vondelpark, perfect for a picnic after the Albert Cuypmarkt.

name: Stach Food
notes: Beloved Amsterdam deli-café chain known for beautiful breakfast bowls, sandwiches, and house-made pastries. Several locations across the city.

name: Royal Palace Amsterdam
notes: The 17th-century City Hall turned royal palace on Dam Square, one of the finest classical buildings in the world. Lavish interiors with Rembrandt-era art.
